title: IS12:: av_line_while.c (118.1)

lines.explanation: Variable c has to be defined as an integer since it may get EOF value as a result if the assignment below. EOF (usually, -1)  is not a char value.
Variable nc is defined as long to enable us to count symbols in large files.
Another way to to it would be nl = nc = 0;

This is a standatd way in C to read a sequence of characters. Variable c gets the value (code) of the new character from the standard input to be processed. This value is also returned as the value of (c = getchar()) expression. It is them compared with E
This line will be executed only when c is the newline symbol - i.e., once for every new line.
If nl is still 0 (i.e., there were no lines of input) we will not execute the following statement and will avoid a division by zero error.

lines.code: printf("Average line length is %.2f\n", nc / (float) nl);
lines.explanation: Since both nc and nl are integral type variables, we need to use expplicit casting to avoid integer division. We want a floating point result that will give us a more precise value for the average line lengh.
